To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the GOOSC is an example of a successful international program that has provided real-time, in situ, global ocean observations for over a decade and has been used to improve weather and climate forecasts.

the use of the Global Ocean Observing Systems (GOOS) has been shown to improve the quality of the forecasts of NOAA's weather and climate models, and that the use of GOOS data in the verification of model forecasts has been shown to increase the understanding of the ocean and its role in the climate system.
the GOOSC has been successful in operating two global networks for more than 20 years and has learned many valuable lessons in operating these networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of mesoscale eddies on the large-scale circulation, and how they influence the climate of the world ocean.
developing and testing new methods of data analysis, and with developing new observing systems and platforms.
the development and application of numerical techniques for solving the equations of motion of a viscous, incompressible fluid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
operating global observing networks is a complex and challenging endeavor that requires international cooperation, and a significant investment of time and money.
the operation and maintenance of a global observing system is not a trivial undertaking and requires significant resources, both in terms of funding and personnel.
the GOOSC is an example of how a small, dedicated group of individuals can operate and manage global observing networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the GOOS Center has been a success in that we have been able to provide the operational data needed by the weather forecasters, the research data needed by the climate forecasters, and the data needed to improve the quality of our observations and models.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of a global observing system for the ocean and atmosphere and have shown the utility and benefits of such a system.
the GOOSC has demonstrated that it can provide a cost effective means of operating a global observing system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to be effective, a global ocean observing system must have a global perspective and a global reach.

, because of the cost of operating a global observing network, international participation is critical; that data management methodology is an essential component of operations; integrated observing systems using a mix of platforms provide more accurate products than single platforms; and that data assimilation systems provide a means to integrate data from multiple sources.

the data collected by these observing systems are essential to the development, validation, and improvement of numerical weather and climate models, and to the development and improvement of the understanding of the ocean and the atmosphere.
